problem: fetch_report passes a URL the caller controls straight to requests.get. The diff removed both the ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist and the fixed https://api.internal.example base, so this is a full SSRF.
failure: fetch_report('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/'), or 'http://localhost:6379/', or 'http://10.0.0.5/admin': the server fetches the internal resource and returns resp.content to the caller. That leaks cloud credentials or internal data and lets a caller scan internal ports.
fix: Restore the fixed base URL and treat the input as a path, or validate the URL: require https, check the host against an allowlist, resolve it and reject private, loopback and link-local IPs, connect to the pinned IP, and set allow_redirects=False or re-validate each redirect hop.

problem: The scheme is no longer forced to https. Plain http:// URLs are accepted, so report fetches lose TLS.
failure: fetch_report('http://api.internal.example/report') sends the request and response in cleartext. A network attacker can read or change report bytes that the old code always fetched over HTTPS.
fix: Reject any scheme other than https, or build the URL from a fixed https base.

problem: resp.content reads the whole response into memory with no size cap. timeout=10 limits each socket read, not the whole transfer. Now that arbitrary hosts are accepted, an attacker controls the response.
failure: An attacker URL serves a multi-GB body, or sends 1 byte every 9 seconds. The worker runs out of memory or is held indefinitely, which is a DoS.
fix: Use stream=True, read in chunks up to a maximum byte count, and enforce a deadline on the total transfer time.

problem: Breaking API change: the parameter changed from a relative path joined to a fixed base URL to a full user_url. Existing callers that pass paths now break.
failure: fetch_report('reports/2026-q3.pdf') now raises requests.exceptions.MissingSchema instead of fetching https://api.internal.example/reports/2026-q3.pdf.
fix: Keep the path-based signature and the fixed base URL.
